actions.action: Peel off the dry sheath from the cutting
Recut cutting cleanly about 1 cm below the node
Remove 1-2 oldest leaves if cutting is top-heavy
Place cutting in jar of water with node submerged in bright indirect light
If cut end turns soft/black/slimy, recut above it
Pot up rooted cutting in small pot with peat/coir mix
Alternatively tuck rooted cutting back into mother pot
Keep new plant's soil lightly moist for first weeks
Trim floppy stems of mother plant above a node
Alternatively stake the stems of the mother plant
Move plant to brighter indirect light if growth is leggy

reason: The answer correctly identifies a broken red maranta cutting with a node and recommends rooting it in water with weekly water changes, matching the fix, with no harmful advice.
